dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real square matrix A indexed by a finite type ι, there exist real numbers λ_p and an ι-indexed basis (b_p) of the real vector space ι → ℝ such that A b_p = λ_p b_p for every p.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires a real eigenbasis for the 1 × 1 matrix [coefficient(x)] at every real x. The eigenvalues and basis may depend on x.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every function u : ℝ → ℝ and every x,s ∈ ℝ, if u has derivative s at x, then y ↦ flux(y,u(y)) has derivative coefficient(x)s at x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target denies the existence of any single flux satisfying this implication for all profiles, points, and derivative values.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Maps a real number a to the matrix indexed by Fin 1 in both coordinates whose sole entry is a.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The matrix condition concerns exactly [coefficient(x)], acting on a one-dimensional real vector space.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: Asserts continuity of the real scalar action on ℝ, namely joint continuity of real multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides structural continuity needed to interpret the derivative predicate; it adds no assumption on the coefficient or flux.

binders: There exists a single coefficient a : ℝ → ℝ.
The positivity and matrix clauses each quantify over every x ∈ ℝ.

For each x, the matrix clause existentially quantifies λ : Fin 1 → ℝ and a basis b indexed by Fin 1 of the real vector space Fin 1 → ℝ, then universally quantifies p ∈ Fin 1. These witnesses may depend on x and a.
For the selected a, there does not exist F : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ satisfying the specified flux property.
Inside that property, one universally quantifies a profile u : ℝ → ℝ, a point x ∈ ℝ, and a slope s ∈ ℝ. A candidate F must work simultaneously for every such choice.
hypotheses: There are no external hypotheses or universally quantified coefficient parameters.
The flux property is conditional on u having derivative s at x; no global regularity assumption on u is imposed.
conclusions: The coefficient a is infinitely continuously differentiable on all of ℝ.
For every x ∈ ℝ, the real matrix A_x = [a(x)] has a real eigenbasis: there exist λ and b as specified such that A_x b_p = λ_p b_p for every p ∈ Fin 1.
There is no function F : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ such that, for every u : ℝ → ℝ and every x,s ∈ ℝ, u'(x) = s in the sense of existence of the derivative implies that y ↦ F(y,u(y)) has derivative a(x)s at x.
mathematical_definitions: Fin 1 = {0}; the vector space Fin 1 → ℝ has dimension one.
A_x(i,j) = a(x) for the sole pair i = j = 0, and (A_x v)(0) = a(x)v(0).
A real eigenbasis is a linearly independent spanning family of real vectors satisfying the displayed eigenvector equations; it is not required to be orthonormal.
The differentiability order is some(∞) in WithTop ENat, expressing C∞ regularity rather than selection of the separate analytic branch.
HasDerivAt g t x means that the ordinary two-sided derivative of g at x exists and equals t.
The flux property differentiates the full composition y ↦ F(y,u(y)), including the variation of F's first argument.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There exists a smooth function a : ℝ → ℝ that is strictly positive everywhere and whose associated 1 × 1 matrix [a(x)] admits a real eigenbasis at every real x, but for which no single function F : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ has the following property: for every real-valued profile u on ℝ, at every point x where u has derivative s, the function y ↦ F(y,u(y)) has derivative a(x)s at x.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The coefficient, profiles, and flux are defined globally on real domains; there is no restricted interval, boundary, or exceptional set of points.
The matrix dimension is fixed at one. Every real 1 × 1 matrix has a real eigenbasis, so this clause imposes no additional restriction on a.
Fin 1 is nonempty, and a basis vector is nonzero; the eigenbasis clause is not satisfied by an empty family or by choosing zero eigenvectors.
Eigenvalue and basis witnesses are pointwise. Their continuity, smoothness, normalization, and uniform bounds are not required.
Strict positivity is pointwise; no positive uniform lower bound or upper bound is specified.
Profiles need only be differentiable at the tested point. For a profile, point, and slope not satisfying the derivative premise, the implication imposes no requirement.
The derivative premise is not universally vacuous: affine profiles realize every prescribed value and slope at every point.

The excluded flux ranges over all functions of two real arguments, without a separately imposed continuity or differentiability class. The required composite derivatives are part of the excluded property itself.
A flux cannot be chosen separately for each profile or point: it must satisfy the universal property for the fixed coefficient.

The statement supplies no explicit coefficient formula and does not explicitly assert nonconstancy. Nonconstancy follows from the nonexistence clause, since a constant coefficient c admits F(x,z) = cz.
No differential equation, time variable, solution class, integral conservation statement, weak formulation, or boundary condition is encoded.
